name: Utlyze Security Report Connector
author: Utlyze

sections.description:
Utlyze Security Report Connector is for owners who bought a Utlyze security report at isyoursitesafe.com. It lets that report see what an outside scan cannot: your WordPress and PHP versions, each installed plugin and theme with its version, update settings and a short list of security settings. SiteSafe then checks those versions against public lists of known security problems.

The plugin is read-only. It never logs in as you, never changes a setting, a file or an update, and never sends anything by itself. Utlyze asks, with a signed request, after you pair the plugin with your report.

This plugin needs the Utlyze security report service, which is paid: it does nothing without a paid Essential or Complete report or plan. Prices: https://isyoursitesafe.com/pricing

External services

This plugin connects your site to the Utlyze security report service at isyoursitesafe.com.

  • What is sent: when the service makes a signed request, the plugin answers with the WordPress and PHP versions, the installed plugins and themes with their versions and update settings, admin account counts, whether a login named “admin” exists, and a fixed list of settings. No names, emails, posts, media, passwords, cookies or configuration files are sent.
  • When: only after you paste the one-time pairing code into your Utlyze security report, and only when the service asks. The plugin itself never makes an outbound request.
  • Terms of service: https://isyoursitesafe.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://isyoursitesafe.com/privacy

Privacy and read-only scope

One signed GET endpoint reads WordPress/PHP versions, every installed plugin
and theme, update preferences, admin counts, the presence of the login “admin”,
and a fixed list of settings. It sends no names, emails, posts, media, passwords,
cookies or configuration files. It never makes an outbound request.

The only writes are its own authentication option: a hash of the pairing code,
a hash of a random per-site token, expiration times and replay nonces. This
bookkeeping is required for pairing/replay protection; it changes no site
content, accounts, settings, installed files or updates. No raw token is stored
or transmitted. Treat the stored HMAC key hash as a secret too.

The endpoint cannot write to the site. No application password is requested.
Deleting the plugin through WordPress removes all its state. Removing its
folder directly does not execute WordPress’s uninstall hook.

XML-RPC output is the authenticated-methods preference, not a network test.
Auto-update flags do not prove a working scheduler or host-managed updates.

sections.installation:
Upload the utlyze-security-report-connector.zip file at Plugins > Add New Plugin > Upload Plugin,
activate it, and paste the one-time code and inventory URL into your Utlyze security report.
The code appears once and expires after 10 minutes. Deactivate and reactivate
to replace a lost/expired code or revoke and replace a connection.
The plugin refuses non-HTTPS connections and multisite installations.
